column1: *** AND THE INITIAL IS J, NOT I ***
column2: this archive's own note read it as "LuwinSki, I." from the OCR. THE PAGE SHOWS A CAPITAL J IN FRAKTUR. Small, and it matters: JOACHIM LUWINSKI, born Allenstein 21 October 1865, would have been forty-seven. NOT PROVED. A directory gives an initial, not a man.

column1: what INVALIDE means
column2: not "invalid" in the English sense of sickly. In Prussian usage it is a status: a man drawing a disability or veteran's pension, no longer in his trade. Joachim Luwinski is recorded elsewhere as a LANDWIRT — a farmer. A farmer who has stopped farming and lives in a Berlin tenement is the shape of that word.

column1: *** AND THE NEXT HOUSE ALONG ***
column2: 31 E Huschert, C., Eigentüm. (Nr. 14). B. 9. ... Köhler, R., Bandagist. · Koeltlitz, W., Beleuchter. · *** LEIBHOLZ, G., KFM. *** · Liebenhagen, W., Maurer. · Liedtke, M., Ww.

column1: so, plainly
column2: IN THE WINTER OF 1912-13 A LUWINSKI HOUSEHOLD AND A LEIBHOLZ HOUSEHOLD WERE LIVING NEXT DOOR TO EACH OTHER. Auguste Luwinski married Jacob Leibholz on 5 January 1924. Her son Kurt was born on 11 May 1912.

column1: # ---------------- WHICH STREET, AND HOW THAT WAS SETTLED ----------------
the street
column2: *** CHODOWIECKISTRASSE, BERLIN N 55 *** — Prenzlauer Berg.

column1: how it was settled rather than assumed
column2: the street's own heading is on the PREVIOUS page, 138, and was cropped and read: "NO. 55 · CHODOWIECKISTR. · A.G. Berl. Mitte. — L.G. I · Dan. Nikol. Chodowiecki, Maler u. Kupferstecher, geb. 16.10.1726, † 7.2.1801." The house numbers run unbroken from 1 on page 138 through 22, 26, 29, 30, 31, 32, 33, 35, 37 to 40 on page 139, and the street ends at an arrow marked "← Greifswalder Str. →", immediately after which a new heading reads "N.37 CHORINER STR."

column1: and the corner confirms it
column2: number 32 is marked "s. a. Winsstr. 42" and number 33 "s. a. Winsstr. 33" — consecutive numbers on opposite sides of the same junction, which is what Berlin numbering does where a street meets another. CHODOWIECKISTRASSE CROSSES WINSSTRASSE. The building was a corner house.

column1: why the street had to be proved at all
column2: the page's running heads are "Chodowieckistr." and "Choriner Str.", and a running head names the first and last street on a page, not the street a given column belongs to. Reading a house number off one column and a street name off the header is exactly the two-adjacent-entries error this archive made with the 1969 estate notice. It was not made again.

column1: *** IT DATES TO THE YEAR KURT WAS BORN ***
column2: the Berliner Adressbuch for 1913 was compiled in the AUTUMN OF 1912. Kurt Luwinski was born on 11 May 1912. THIS IS WHERE THE LUWINSKI HOUSEHOLD WAS IN THE YEAR OF HIS BIRTH, give or take a removal.

column1: and it gives a district, which is the thing that was missing
column2: Kurt's birth registry office has never been known, and the Berlin name indexes are organised by office. PRENZLAUER BERG, N 55, NARROWS TWENTY-ONE CANDIDATE VOLUMES TO A HANDFUL. Which of the old Roman-numeral Standesämter served Chodowieckistraße in 1912 IS NOT YET ESTABLISHED and is not guessed at here.

column1: and it may be how the two families met
column2: this is the honest shape of it. A LUWINSKI AT NUMBER 32 AND A LEIBHOLZ AT NUMBER 31. Eleven years later a Luwinski daughter married a Leibholz son. NOTHING HERE PROVES THE TWO HOUSEHOLDS ARE THOSE FAMILIES, and both surnames are borne by other people in Berlin. What it does is give the marriage a plausible geography for the first time, and give the archive a specific address to test against every other source it holds.

column1: what would test it
column2: the 1912 and 1914 volumes at the same page. Neither could be pinned today: the OCR carries "Luwinski" in 1913 alone, exact searches return nothing in the neighbouring years, and a fuzzy search returns forty-four hits an edit away — Lewinski, Lawinski and the rest — which is a list to work through, not an answer. THE PAGE HAS TO BE FOUND BY STREET, NOT BY NAME, AND THAT IS THE NEXT JOB.

column1: # ---------------- AND THE NEIGHBOUR HAS A NAME: THE SAME VOLUME'S NAME SECTION ----------------
*** GEORG LEIBHOLZ ***
column2: Berliner Adressbuch 1913, Teil I, the Leibholz run: "— GEORG, KAUFM., NO 55, CHODOWIECKISTR. 31 II." Read at the image. The street entry's "Leibholz, G., Kfm." at number 31 is GEORG LEIBHOLZ, a merchant, ON THE SECOND FLOOR, and the Luwinskis were at number 32.

column1: and this archive already has a Georg
column2: GEORG LEIBHOLZ, born at HAMMERSTEIN, whom the Bundesarchiv Gedenkbuch gives and whom this archive established CANNOT BE JACOB'S BROTHER — born two months apart in two different towns. He has his own lane on the register of lines. WHETHER HE IS THIS MAN IS NOT ESTABLISHED. The 1913 volume lists exactly one Georg Leibholz in Berlin, which is suggestive and is not proof.

column1: *** AND JAQUES IS TWO LINES BELOW HIM ***
column2: — JAQUES, KAUFM., W 62, LUTHERSTR. 34 II. THE MAN AUGUSTE MARRIED ELEVEN YEARS LATER IS IN THE SAME COLUMN OF THE SAME PAGE, four lines down from the man living next door to her family.

column1: a new address for Jacob, and the earliest there is
column2: this archive's earliest address for him was Meraner Straße 2 in the 1938 directory and the 1939 census. LUTHERSTRASSE 34, W 62, IN 1913 IS TWENTY-FIVE YEARS EARLIER.

column1: *** AND IT IS NOT THE STREET HIS SON WAS BORN IN. CHECKED THE SAME DAY AND THE GUESS IS DEAD. ***
column2: this file first said that Lutherstraße "may be" the street later called MARTIN-LUTHER-STRASSE, where Siegfried was born in 1925, and flagged it unverified. IT IS NOW VERIFIED AND IT IS WRONG. Berlin's Martin-Luther-Straße in Schöneberg has carried that name SINCE 28 DECEMBER 1899, and its only earlier names were HEINRICH-KIEPERT-STRASSE (1893-1899) and ROSTOCKER STRASSE (1884-1893). It was never a Lutherstraße. The only Lutherstraße in Berlin today is in STEGLITZ, formerly Grabenstraße. Source: the Berlin street lexicon at berlin.kauperts.de, both entries read 20 September 2026.

column1: and the refutation is worth more than the guess was
column2: Jaques Leibholz's 1913 address is in postal district W 62 — BERLIN PROPER. Schöneberg was a separate city until it was absorbed into Groß-Berlin in 1920 and had its own postal districts. SO IN 1913 HE WAS NOT LIVING IN SCHÖNEBERG AT ALL. The family's arrival there is a real move, not a continuity, and the marriage at Schöneberg II in January 1924 marks the end of it rather than the middle. Where W 62's Lutherstraße went is not established: it is not an earlier name of any street kauperts lists, so it was absorbed or renumbered, and that is a separate question.

column1: and one more spelling for the register
column2: the same page carries the cross-reference "LEIPHOLZ, s. a. LEIBHOLZ". *** LEIPHOLZ. *** An eighth spelling, printed by the directory itself, and one this archive has never searched anywhere.

column1: # ---------------- THE VOLUMES EITHER SIDE, READ THE SAME DAY ----------------
*** 1912: THE HOUSE DID NOT EXIST YET ***
column2: the 1912 volume, Teil III, printed page 140, gives "32 NEUBAU. E. BERL. TERRAIN-GESELLSCHAFT" and then the arrow to Winsstraße. A NEW BUILDING, still owned by the development company, with no tenants at all. By the 1913 volume it has been sold to Arend and filled.

column1: *** 1912: AND NO LEIBHOLZ NEXT DOOR EITHER ***
column2: number 31 in 1912 runs Huschert the owner, then Abraham, Anders, Böttger, Coper, Falke, Frank, Fürstenberg, Gaedtke, Gronwald, Hartwig, Hempel, Kahn, Kersten, Köhler, Koettlitz, KRINKE, Liebenhagen, Liedtke. In 1913 the same run reads Köhler, Koeltlitz, LEIBHOLZ, Liebenhagen, Liedtke. GEORG LEIBHOLZ MOVED IN DURING 1912.

column1: *** 1914: THE LUWINSKIS ARE GONE AND THE LEIBHOLZ IS STILL THERE ***
column2: 1914, Teil III, printed page 143. Number 31 still carries "Leibholz, G., Kfm." Number 32 runs Arand the owner, Lorenz, Behrendt, Damm, Franz, Gelsky, Grünberg, Heiber, Jürgens, Krug, Krüger, LANDOW, MICHAELIS, Muth, Niedergesäß, Pahlke, Ritter, Schulze, Seiffert, Siggelkow, Walter, Wrus, Zwieg. IN AN ALPHABETICAL LIST, LUWINSKI WOULD STAND BETWEEN LANDOW AND MICHAELIS. IT IS NOT THERE.

column1: so the tenancy is one volume wide
column2: the Luwinski household appears at Chodowieckistraße 32 in the 1913 volume and in no other. They moved into a brand-new building some time in 1912 and were gone again before the autumn of 1913. ONE YEAR, CAUGHT BY ONE BOOK.

column1: # ---------------- AND THAT WEAKENS THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN CORROBORATION ----------------
*** SAID EARLIER TODAY, AND IT NEEDS QUALIFYING ***
column2: the file data/kurt-birth-entry.tsv says "four things agree" for the identification of Kurt's birth entry, and counts the DISTRICT as one of the four. The district came from this address. BUT THE ADDRESS IS FROM A BOOK COMPILED IN THE AUTUMN OF 1912 AND THE BIRTH WAS IN MAY 1912 — and it is now known that the family had moved into that building at some point during that very year.

column1: what that does and does not do
column2: IT DOES NOT TOUCH THE ENTRY ITSELF. The index of Standesamt Berlin VIII for 1912 was opened and read, and it contains a LUWINSKI, forename KURT, in the MAY block, at number 963, and exactly one Luwinski in the whole year. Those are facts about the register, not about the directory. THE DISTRICT WAS THE REASON FOR OPENING THAT VOLUME, NOT PART OF THE PROOF.

column1: the honest count is therefore three and a half
column2: surname, forename and month agree outright. The district agrees on a reading that puts the family in Standesamt 8 by the autumn of 1912 and cannot show where they were in May. The certificate settles it; the address on it is one of the things most worth having.

column1: # ---------------- ONE CORRECTION TO THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN FILE ----------------
data/berlin-adressbuch.tsv
column2: its Luwinski table reads "1913 · LuwinSki, I., Invalide." WITHOUT AN ADDRESS. That line is now superseded: the initial is J and the address is Chodowieckistraße 32, corner of Winsstraße, Berlin N 55.

column1: and the general lesson, which this archive keeps relearning
column2: A TEXT-LAYER HIT IS NOT A READ ENTRY. The OCR gave a name and swallowed the street, the house number, the neighbour and the initial. Everything of value on that page was in the four lines the search result did not show.
